observations: Photo 0 shows a black DSLR camera body with 'Nikon' and 'D5' clearly visible on the top front.
The camera has a lens cap with 'Nikon' written on it, and an 'FX' badge on the front right side.
Photo 1 shows the back of the camera with a large LCD screen, smaller secondary screen, and various control buttons. 'Nikon D5' is visible below the main screen.
Photo 2 shows the top-left side of the camera, including the mode dial, hot shoe, and top LCD screen. The body appears to have some dust or speckles.
All photos show the camera on a dark surface with a striped background and a sign that says 'OYI-BEST CAMERAS'.
No lens is attached to the camera in any photo.
The camera body appears to be in used condition with minor surface marks and dust.

claims.claim: Nikon D5 is a professional flagship full-frame (FX-format) DSLR camera built for extreme speed
claims.evidence: The 'FX' badge is visible on the front of the camera in photo 0, and the model 'D5' is clearly readable in photo 0 and photo 1. The D5 is known as a professional flagship model.

risks.risk: Camera may not be functional or may have internal damage (e.g., sensor, shutter, or electronics)
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on, menu navigation, and shutter operation, or a photo of the camera with a lens attached and a test shot displayed on the screen.

risks.risk: Camera may have hidden physical damage (e.g., cracked body, damaged ports, or internal components)
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all ports, buttons, dials, and seams, especially around the hot shoe, battery compartment, and lens mount.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential hidden damage

risks.risk: Camera may be stolen or have a compromised serial number (common in second-hand markets)
risks.proof: Photo of the serial number plate on the camera body, preferably with a clear, unobstructed view.
risks.if_unproven: priced with reduced value due to provenance risk

proof_requests: Video or photo showing the camera powering on and operating (menu, shutter, LCD).
Close-up photos of all ports, buttons, and the lens mount.
Photo of the serial number plate on the camera body.
response.reason: The camera is clearly identified as a Nikon D5, and the seller's claim is supported by visible branding and model markings. However, functionality, physical condition, and provenance cannot be verified from the current photos. Without proof of operation and condition, the item must be priced at its worst case, which requires additional evidence.
